executive_summary: TechCorp's Information Security Policy partially aligns with the National Cryptographic Standards, demonstrating a good understanding of symmetric encryption standards and asymmetric key exchange. However, several areas of non-compliance were identified, including the reuse of Initialization Vectors for stream ciphers, the use of RSA with a 2048-bit key length, and the utilization of SHA-2 for digital signatures and integrity. To achieve full compliance, TechCorp must address these violations and implement the recommended changes. Overall, the company's policy requires significant revisions to meet the national standards.
compliant_areas: Utilization of AES with a 128-bit key length for standard data encryption (Section 2.1.2 of the framework context)
Use of Serpent with a 256-bit key for Advanced level storage (Section 2.1.2 of the framework context)
Employment of Elliptic Curve (ECC) based on NIST P-521 for Advanced zone communications (Section 2.2 of the framework context)
violations: Reuse of Initialization Vectors for stream ciphers, violating the requirement for a unique IV for each key (Section 2.1.1 of the framework context)
Use of RSA with a 2048-bit key length, which is below the recommended 3072 bits for MODERATE (Section 2.2 of the framework context)
Utilization of SHA-2 (SHA2-384) for digital signatures, which is not accepted for ADVANCED (Section 2.3 of the framework context)
Use of SHA-2 (SHA2-512/256) for Advanced zone integrity, which is not accepted for ADVANCED (Section 2.3 of the framework context)
Employment of SHAKE128 with an output size (d value) of 128 bits, which is below the recommended 256 bits (Section 2.3 of the framework context)
Use of SOSEMANUK stream cipher with a 256-bit key for Advanced zone, which is not accepted for ADVANCED (Section 2.1.1 of the framework context)
recommendations: Implement a unique Initialization Vector for each key, as required by Section 2.1.1 of the framework context
Upgrade RSA key length to at least 3072 bits for MODERATE, as specified in Section 2.2 of the framework context
Replace SHA-2 with SHA-3 for digital signatures and integrity, as recommended in Section 2.3 of the framework context
Increase the output size (d value) of SHAKE128 to at least 256 bits, as specified in Section 2.3 of the framework context
Replace SOSEMANUK stream cipher with a accepted algorithm for ADVANCED, such as SNOW 2.0 or AES, as listed in Section 2.1.1 of the framework context
